stages.title: Brief
stages.goal: Your brief, word for word.

stages.title: Restate the brief
stages.goal: Restate in plain English what the operator wants built and why, and what is out of scope. Show it to the operator.

stages.title: Research
stages.goal: Write docs/01-research.md.

stages.title: Value map
stages.goal: Write docs/02-value-map.md.

stages.title: PRD
stages.goal: Write docs/03-prd.md.

stages.title: Architecture
stages.skill: saas-architecture-fit (pstack architect when the design is contested)
stages.goal: Write docs/04-architecture.md.

stages.title: Similar products and inspiration
stages.goal: Capture 3-5 current competitors and 2 roundups + 2 Dribbble searches (capture-herd, harvest-roundup, capture-gallery).

stages.title: Reference contact sheets
stages.goal: Numbered contact sheets of REAL screenshots (data URIs; open the JPG and confirm every tile shows a picture), one per surface.

stages.title: Pick the references
stages.question: Which number for web and console?

stages.title: Teardown from the picked image
stages.goal: Frontmatter picked_by: operator + the operator's words from the gate. Rows describe what is VISIBLE in the picked image (ground, type, art medium, shape) before any word of ours.

stages.title: Extract the look
stages.goal: extract-look.mjs on the picked reference(s).

stages.title: Find the assets
stages.goal: Every asset slot of the reference's first three screens, found (never invented), with source, credit, licence. Different art medium than the reference: stop and say so.

stages.title: Palette options
stages.goal: Three whole palettes (or the reference's own when the operator asked for it), each shown on the reference's layout.

stages.title: Palette and theme
stages.goal: palette.json (picked_by: operator, words from the gate), then derive-theme --palette.

stages.title: Prototype variants
stages.goal: 2-3 hero + first-section variants moulded from the picked reference, in the theme, with the assets; one sheet showing each BESIDE the reference.

stages.title: Approve a prototype
stages.question: Which variant looks like your pick?

stages.title: Lock the design contract
stages.goal: design-contract.mjs <product>; the approved variant is the baseline the build must match.

stages.title: Verification skill
stages.goal: A control CLI that serves, drives and screenshots each surface, and a feature map (one file per screen) under verify/.

stages.title: Scaffold
stages.goal: scaffold-surface.mjs <product> web; scaffold-surface.mjs <product> console

stages.title: Feature specs
stages.goal: One spec per feature; each task has a VERIFY line that runs the control CLI. Queue files in specs/queue/ (orch format). Run: parallel.

stages.title: Build the specs
stages.goal: Build each queued spec; orch (or you) runs them. Write specs/queue/.done when every spec is merged.

stages.title: Parity: web
stages.goal: compare-to.mjs <web url> design/prototype/approved-web.html --out design/review/parity-web; fix until it matches.

stages.title: Accept web
stages.question: Does the built web match your pick?

stages.title: Parity: console
stages.goal: compare-to.mjs <console url> design/prototype/approved-console.html --out design/review/parity-console; fix until it matches.

stages.title: Accept console
stages.question: Does the built console match your pick?

stages.title: Review
stages.goal: One fresh-context pass, at most 2 rounds; findings fixed or closed with a reason, written to design/review/review.md.

now.title: Restate the brief
now.goal: Restate in plain English what the operator wants built and why, and what is out of scope. Show it to the operator.
